newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to emphasise Brazilian sales.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to emphasise Brazilian sales.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Monday it is attaching importance to creating a powerful sales network in Brazil as a part of its worldwide strategy.

Mazda moved a step forward in strengthening its Brazilian sales in April when it shifted business of importing and distributing Mazda cars from a local independent company to Itochu Corp's Brazilian unit, a Mazda spokesman said.
Itochu has close ties with Mazda, owning a 5.08 percent in the car maker's U.S. sales unit and 40 percent in Mazda's Canadian sales unit.
Mazda's exports to Brazil stood at 3,066 in calendar 1996, little changed from the previous year, the spokesman said.
Mazda has no production unit in Brazil.

In a concession last year, Brazil created a quota system under which carmakers from the European Union, Japan and South Korea are allowed to export a total of 50,000 cars a year to Brazil at a 35 percent tariff rate.
Brazil has a restrictive car import policy.
